growing_specifications.description: High-value, fast-cycling crisp leafy salad vegetable cultivated extensively in Philippine highland terraces (Benguet, Mountain Province, Bukidnon) and cool-season lowland raised beds. Features shallow root systems, high moisture requirements, and sensitivity to heat-induced bolting.

category_why.title: Why is Lettuce classified under Salad Greens (Asteraceae)?
category_why.summary: Lactuca sativa belongs to the Asteraceae (sunflower) family, growing in a compact rosette of tender, crisp leaves harvested prior to the reproductive bolting phase.
points: Compact Rosette Growth: Forms a 15–25 cm wide low-lying cluster of succulent leaves packed with water (95%) and fiber.
Vegetative Harvest Priority: Harvested strictly during the vegetative stage before central stem elongation and flower bud development.
Rapid Lifecycle: Completes emergence to harvest maturity in 55 to 70 days, ideal for intensive sequential cropping cycles.

harvest_why.title: Why is harvest maturity timed to 55–70 days before bolting?
harvest_why.summary: Harvesting at full rosette expansion preserves crispness, tenderness, and natural sweetness before temperatures trigger bitter lactucarium sap.
points: Germination & Emergence (Days 3–7): Fine seeds sprout rapidly under shallow 0.5 cm sowing.
Nursery Tray Establishment (Days 7–25): Seedlings develop 3–4 true leaves in 104-hole trays before transplanting.
Rosette Expansion (Days 25–50): Rapid leaf expansion and heart formation supported by consistent soil moisture.
Peak Market Maturity (Days 55–70): Rosettes reach 300–600 g per head with crisp, tender, sweet leaves.
Bolting Risk Post-70 Days: Temperatures exceeding 28–30°C induce central stalk elongation, tough foliage, and unpalatable bitter milky sap.

watering_why.title: Why does Lettuce require daily to alternate-day light irrigation?
watering_why.summary: With 95% moisture content and a shallow fibrous root zone (5–15 cm), lettuce cannot tolerate dry topsoil without wilting and bittering.
points: Shallow Root Vulnerability: Fibrous feeder roots occupy only the top 10 cm of soil, rapidly exhausting surface moisture.
Lactucarium & Bitterness Prevention: Water stress immediately triggers defense alkaloids that make salad greens astringent and bitter.
Tip-Burn Suppression: Steady transpiration flow is required to transport immobile calcium to expanding inner leaf margins.

soil_why.title: Why does Lettuce prefer well-drained loam with pH 6.0–6.8 on raised beds?
soil_why.summary: Requires loose, humus-rich soil for delicate feeder roots and 15–20 cm bed elevation to prevent waterlogging and soft rot.
points: Drainage & Aeration: Raised beds prevent root asphyxiation and damping-off during tropical rain downpours.
Nutrient Absorption: pH 6.0–6.8 optimizes uptake of Nitrogen (100–150 kg/ha) for fast leaf formation and Calcium to prevent tip-burn.
Bottom Rot Prevention: Mulched raised beds keep lower leaves elevated away from muddy, pathogen-laden soil.

varieties.description: Leading commercial loose-leaf cultivar in the Philippines with light green, deeply frilled crisp leaves, high heat tolerance, and cut-and-come-again harvesting suitability.
Classic crisphead (iceberg) variety grown extensively in Benguet highland farms (Atok, La Trinidad). Forms dense, firm 400–600 g heads with crunchy, sweet leaves.
Upright, heat-tolerant Romaine/Cos lettuce with thick, sweet ribs and dark green outer leaves. Highly adaptable to lowland cool-season garden beds.
Specialty frilly loose-leaf with stunning burgundy-red leaf edges rich in anthocyanin antioxidants. Slow to bolt and high culinary market value.
